newsitem.title: POLAND: CONSORTIUM TO LAUNCH POLISH GRAIN TERMINAL IN 1998.
newsitem.headline: CONSORTIUM TO LAUNCH POLISH GRAIN TERMINAL IN 1998.

text.p: U.S.-Canadian consortium Europort Inc. is likely to open a $145 million grain terminal in the Baltic city of Gdansk in the second half of 1998, Europort's president said on Tuesday.

The terminal, with an annual loading capacity of three million metric tons of grain and fodder, would mainly serve to unload U.S. and Canadian grain and fodder exported to the former Soviet Union states, Joseph D'Andrea told a news conference.
"In two or three weeks we will apply for a permit for the terminal construction, which should start in the autumn," D'Andrea said, adding that the facility was likely to completed 12 months later.

Europort's shareholders include major Canadian grain producer and exporter Saskatchewan Wheat Pool , as well as consulting firm Dessaport Corp. International and the U.S.-based D'Andrea's own development company.
Last year, when Europort signed an agreement with the Polish port of Gdansk to build the terminal, it said the facility required an investment of $140 million.
It said at the time that the terminal would accept ships up to a maximum 150,000 dead-weight tonnes (dwt).

D'Andrea said that even though Europort had secured financing for the terminal it was in talks with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) on a loan or an equity investment in the venture.
